name: Sara Blakely
why_selected: Shape 1 career-switcher: seven years selling fax machines at Danka, then founded a shapewear company with no prior apparel employment. Stresses a3_first_domain_job.

name: Katalin Kariko
why_selected: Shape 2 research scientist: tests the prize equivalent, and an unusually long education-to-hit clock (40 years).

name: Tadashi Yanai
why_selected: Shape 3 non-US operator: Japanese-language sources, plus an inherited family firm that stresses 'the person's own venture'.

name: Gordon Moore
why_selected: Shape 4 pre-1980 hit: tests whether a 1950s-70s career can be sourced, and whether an earlier venture's revenue crossing can be dated at all.

name: Bong Joon-ho
why_selected: Shape 5 media creator: tests the aud1m equivalent on an artistic work rather than a company.

name: Mary Meeker
why_selected: Shape 6 investor: tests fund100 on someone who was famous for 20 years before closing a fund of her own.

name: Kevin Systrom
why_selected: Shape 7 private company with undisclosed revenue: tests the acq50 fallback path.

name: Robin Li
why_selected: Shape 8 documented $10M revenue: chosen because Baidu's SEC F-1 audits revenue for 2002-2004, which should have made the rev10 primary path trivial.

name: Daniel Ek
why_selected: Shape 9 university dropout: left KTH after eight weeks, so a2_education_end has no tertiary credential.

name: Zhang Yin
why_selected: Shape 10 thinnest bucket: scrap-paper import/export operator, pre-internet career, largely Chinese-language sourcing.

name: Stephanie Shirley
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: founded a freelance software house in 1962 staffed by women programmers working from home. Expect a 1970s crossing, and a real chance the row is undatable because the firm was private and the software trade press did not yet exist.

name: Judy Faulkner
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: Epic from 1979, never venture-funded and never listed, so the crossing may only be bounded. Expect the 1980s. Also the wave's longest single-venture career.

name: Dietmar Hopp
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: five IBM engineers left to start SAP in 1972, which puts a real employment apprenticeship in front of the venture. Expect a mid-to-late 1970s crossing. Sampled off the German end of the list rather than the more-cited co-founder.

name: Kazuhiko Nishi
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: ASCII from 1977 plus the Microsoft Japan tie-up. Expect an early-1980s crossing. Tests Japanese-language sourcing on a listed company whose founder is better documented abroad than at home.

name: Sandra Kurtzig
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit in a rare cell -- a woman founding enterprise software in 1972. ASK's 1981 IPO prospectus should carry revenue back several years, so expect a datable late-1970s crossing rather than an exclusion.

name: Shola Akinlade
why_selected: Emerging-market row: Paystack's reported $200M acquisition exercises acq50 outside the US. Tests whether Nigerian coverage establishes an earlier crossing that bars the fallback.

name: Shigenobu Nagamori
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: Nidec founded 1973 with three employees after years as a motor engineer. Expect a crossing around the turn of the 1980s, sourced from Japanese listing history.

name: Morris Chang
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit and the wave's longest apprenticeship: 25 years at Texas Instruments before founding TSMC at 55 in 1987. Directly stresses what the a3-to-a5 clock is supposed to measure.

name: Zhou Qunfei
why_selected: Factory worker to founder with no tertiary credential, so a2_education_end is a school-leaving date. Lens Technology's 2015 listing should bound an early-2000s crossing.

name: An Wang
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit at the far end: Wang Laboratories from 1951. Expect a 1950s or 1960s crossing, which stresses the constant-dollar threshold and the CPI helper harder than any other row in the wave.

name: Kiran Mazumdar-Shaw
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit, non-US woman: Biocon started 1978 in a garage as an enzyme exporter, a decade before anyone called it biotech. Expect a 1980s crossing that pre-IPO sources may only bound.

name: Thomas Struengmann
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: Hexal built privately from 1986 as a generics maker. Expect a late-1980s crossing, with a genuine exclusion risk since Hexal never listed and disclosed nothing before the 2005 sale.

name: Zhong Huijuan
why_selected: Chemistry teacher who founded Hansoh in 1995. The 2019 Hong Kong listing audits only recent years, so the test is whether Chinese-language sources bound a 2000s crossing or leave the row undatable.

name: Alfred Mann
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit and a serial founder, which stresses the rule that the hit must be the person's own venture: Spectrolab from 1956, then implantable devices from 1969. Expect a 1960s first crossing.

name: Karsanbhai Patel
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: a government lab technician who sold Nirma detergent door to door from 1969. Expect a 1970s crossing, sourced decades before the company disclosed anything.

name: Anita Roddick
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: The Body Shop from 1976 and floated in 1984, so UK filings should make the crossing datable rather than bounded. Expect the early 1980s.

name: Kim Sung-joo
why_selected: Korean luxury-import distributor from 1990 who later bought the German brand she had distributed. A pre-1995 crossing is plausible but genuinely unclear, and a private Korean firm of that era may not be datable at all.

name: Rita Levi-Montalcini
why_selected: Pre-1995 by construction -- the 1986 Nobel is the anchor. An extremely long clock, since the nerve growth factor work began in a bedroom laboratory in wartime Italy.

name: Jean-Marie Lehn
why_selected: Pre-1995 by construction (Chemistry, 1987) and a conventional academic ladder, which gives the bucket a clean baseline against the two irregular careers beside it.

name: Tu Youyou
why_selected: The extreme case for the prize criterion: the artemisinin work dates to the early 1970s and the Nobel to 2015. Tests whether 'the year recognition landed' survives landing four decades late.

name: Sonali De Rycker
why_selected: The fund100 half of the bucket, sampled off the European list so the criterion is exercised away from Sand Hill Road. Named general partner on Accel's London funds.

name: Raghuram Rajan
why_selected: The rank1 half: an academic economist with no fund of his own, so fund100 cannot fire and the anchor must come from a published ranking or the row is excluded. Country marked US for the Chicago career, though the RBI governorship is the better-known role.

name: Toni Morrison
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit: expect the aud1m crossing in the late 1970s or 1980s from book sales, years before the 1988 Pulitzer that put her on the list. Tests aud1m on print, where sales are reported inconsistently.

name: Youssou N'Dour
why_selected: Pre-1995 recruit and the hardest audience measurement in the wave: an African star whose 1980s audience was cassettes sold in markets with no published chart. Expect the frame to strain or the row to be excluded.

name: Ryan Petersen
why_selected: The bucket's single row, chosen to be findable on the rank1 volume path since Flexport appears in JOC/PIERS forwarder and NVOCC volume tables. Post-1995 by design: the frame's own note says a pre-1995 pick here would almost certainly fail.
